entries.test: Public adoption, usage, investment, and commercial activity would show whether generative AI suffered a substantial collapse soon after July 2024.
entries.note: The following paragraph clarifies that flame out does not mean disappear completely.

entries.test: Public valuations, funding, spending, and business failures would show whether the generative AI boom began materially unwinding by July 28, 2025.
entries.note: Fully expect expresses a firm forecast, and its deadline has passed.

entries.test: Independent capability evaluations across successive generative AI releases through July 2024 would show whether meaningful improvement had stalled.
Public adoption, retention, revenue, and demonstrated utility as of July 2024 would establish whether any generative AI application had compelling mass-market demand.
entries.note: Killer app has a conventional commercial reading despite lacking a numerical threshold.

entries.test: Reproducible evaluations and documented outputs from contemporary generative AI systems would establish whether they still fabricated information.
Reproducible examples from contemporary generative AI systems would establish whether they still made elementary factual, arithmetic, or logical mistakes.
entries.note: The essay supplies concrete examples that give boneheaded errors a testable reading.

entries.test: Public evidence of defensible technology, exclusive resources, switching costs, or network effects would establish whether any generative AI company had a durable competitive advantage in July 2024.
Contemporaneous surveys and public commentary would show whether recognition of the listed limitations was increasing by July 2024.
entries.note: This concerns expressed public perceptions, which can be assessed without access to private beliefs.
May well lead states a possibility. The accompanying overrated assessment is a value judgment.

entries.test: Public evidence of AI research and commercial development continuing after a generative AI collapse would establish that the collapse did not end the field.
entries.note: The outcome depends on the anticipated collapse, with no deadline specified.
This combines a possibility about popularity with a firm prediction about better techniques. The latter could be graded separately.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and independent evaluations of generative AI overcoming its intrinsic reliability failures would refute the claim that those failures can never be solved.
entries.note: I believe introduces his asserted position rather than an explicit probability.

entries.test: Controlled evaluations comparing familiar tasks with novel tasks and subtly but materially altered variants would establish the claimed performance pattern.
entries.note: The source specifies differences that are both important and subtle; the normalization drops important.

entries.test: Controlled novel-problem evaluations and public mechanistic studies would test whether LLM solutions reflect reasoning or retrieval of answers to similar problems.
entries.note: The parenthetical generalizes the denial of reasoning, but the retrieval assertion describes this particular answer. The normalization generalizes both.

entries.test: Public enterprise surveys, deployment reports, and documented decisions would show whether reliability failures substantially caused Fortune 500 companies to lose confidence in LLMs.
entries.note: Big part is a reasonable reading of the apparent typo bit part in context.
The normalization removes my strong intuition, presenting a qualified personal expectation as categorical.

entries.test: Controlled public evaluations of unaided LLMs detecting and correcting errors in their own outputs would test their capacity to sanity-check their work.
entries.note: Perhaps qualifies whether this is the deepest problem, rather than the asserted inability itself.

entries.test: Public error evaluations and experiments adding or removing verification mechanisms across the named systems would test the universal error claim and its proposed cause.
entries.note: The normalization omits the explicit claim that these systems occasionally defame people.

entries.test: Controlled reasoning and planning evaluations across varying similarity to known training examples would establish whether performance becomes unreliable on novel situations.
entries.note: Highly vulnerable outside familiar situations does not mean working only in familiar situations.

entries.test: Public evaluations and architectural evidence would test whether hallucinations and reasoning failures persist and arise intrinsically from LLM operation.
entries.note: The normalization removes as far as I can tell and omits discomprehensions. The source nevertheless asserts an empirical account of persistent errors.
In the context of how to do better, this prescribes abandonment or integration into more capable systems.

entries.test: Public technical disclosures, research output, resource allocations, and documented internal practices would establish OpenAI's emphasis on scaling and its treatment of symbolic methods.
entries.note: Trying hard to eschew or hide methods describes efforts; the normalization presents avoidance or concealment as accomplished.

entries.test: Public investment allocations and funding decisions in July 2024 would show whether financing strongly favored established scaling approaches over materially different AI techniques.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion gives novelty a concrete referent: algorithmic alternatives to scaling existing LLMs.

entries.test: Major technology companies' public model evaluations, research portfolios, and investment disclosures through July 2024 would establish their convergence on GPT-4-level LLMs and spending on alternatives.
entries.note: The normalization drops the opening for the most part qualification and the explicit shared error limitations.

entries.test: DeepMind's technical reports and descriptions of its Olympiad workflow would establish whether both systems required humans to translate the problem statements into mathematical representations.
entries.note: The human-translation requirement is factual; calling it a serious shortcoming adds an evaluative judgment.

entries.test: Public architecture descriptions and verified mathematical results from DeepMind's systems would establish whether combining neural and symbolic components produced useful results.
entries.note: Can here describes demonstrated capability, rather than an uncertain future possibility.

entries.test: A publicly demonstrated AGI system and its documented architecture would test whether neurosymbolic methods, knowledge infrastructure, and cognitive models are necessary components.
entries.note: The concluding context makes this a claim about requirements for reaching AGI, rather than merely a description of existing systems.

entries.test: A publicly demonstrated AGI achieved without combining neural and symbolic methods would refute the claimed necessity of neurosymbolic AI.
entries.note: This is an undated necessity claim that a decisive counterexample could settle.
